sections.h2: India's scenario population peaks at 1,639 million in 2050, then falls

chart.title: Population is a scenario input, and the path turns down after mid-century
chart.source: CEEW, GCAM-India annexure (Table 8). Post revised 13 August 2026.

sections.means: In one of the model's 32 regions, the scenario population peaks mid-century and then declines, a demographic input that shapes every downstream energy-service demand number in the model.
sections.todo: Check the population path against the latest UN or Census projection before treating any single-decade output as a forecast.

sections.h2: The urban share of India's population rises from 32.7% to 74.4% by 2100

chart.title: Urbanisation is tied to growth, and the urban share keeps climbing to 2100
chart.sub: Urbanisation rate, % of population, selected years.

sections.means: In the India build set up in 2007–09, faster growth pulls people to cities sooner, and the medium-growth case reaches about 50% urban by 2050, so the urban share is an assumption rather than an output.
sections.todo: Test the urbanisation path against recent census urban-share data before relying on its link to economic growth.

sections.h2: Income per head is a scenario input that climbs from 1,617 to 35,811 dollars

chart.title: Per-capita income climbs steeply, and the model takes that growth as an input
chart.sub: Per-capita income, 2015 US dollars, selected years.

sections.means: GDP and population are scenario inputs in GCAM, so the income path is a chosen assumption rather than something the model derives from first principles.
